pathway.title: Infinity Natural Resources, Inc. — Full credit assessment
pathway.question: Should we own this issuer, in which instrument, and why?

runs.text: Reported leverage is low and liquidity is large, but the debt figure leaves out claims that sit beside it. Total debt was USD 538.8 million at 2026-09-30 against trailing EBITDA of USD 435.4 million, 1.24x, or 1.18x net of USD 26.2 million of cash; adding the USD 336.5 million Series A preferred stock at carrying value lifts the ratio to 2.01x, and the USD 706.3 million of redeemable non-controlling interest is the Legacy Owners' claim on the same assets. The issuer reports no EBITDA, so it is operating income plus depreciation, depletion and amortization; it includes the Antero assets only from 2026-02-23 and leaves out USD 19.0 million of net derivative settlement losses over the period. Liquidity of USD 901.2 million is cash plus an undrawn revolver whose size is set by a borrowing base that lenders redetermine twice a year. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation calc-adj-lev; 10-K_2025-12-31_inr-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 75; 10-Q_2026-09-30_inr-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 26–27

Cash generation does not yet cover the growth programme, which is the central weakness. Operating cash flow of USD 408.6 million over the last twelve months fell short of capital expenditure of USD 470.1 million, leaving free cash flow of negative USD 61.6 million before the USD 620.5 million paid for Antero, and management expects financing to keep funding spending through the rest of 2026. About USD 41.9 million a year of coupon on the notes and USD 28.0 million of cash preferred dividends now come before debt reduction. A large part of the spending looks discretionary: developing the proved undeveloped and non-producing reserves needs about USD 737 million over five years, or USD 147.4 million a year, against USD 470.1 million spent, although that figure excludes Antero, midstream and land and 23.23% of undeveloped acreage expires by 2030, which holds some drilling in place. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation calc-fixed; calculation calc-capex-need; calculation calc-acreage; 10-K_2025-12-31_inr-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 23, 51; 10-Q_2026-09-30_inr-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 27, 37, 60

Margins are high and have held through price swings, but they rest on prices the company does not control. EBITDA was 67.97% of revenue over the last twelve months and 66.82% in the first nine months of 2026, against 65.84% in FY2023 and 64.65% in FY2024; FY2025 shows 32.45% because of USD 126.1 million of one-off non-cash IPO share compensation, and 67.82% without it, which is a normalisation by this analysis. Oil supplied 48.46% of nine-month revenue and gas and NGLs 50.14%, and the 2027 hedges cover roughly 39.98% of annualised third-quarter oil volume and 42.63% of gas volume; the hedge book was a net liability of USD 23.1 million, because oil and NGL swaps priced below current benchmarks, such as the 2027 oil swaps at USD 65.08 a barrel against USD 87.22 in the third quarter, outweigh gains on gas swaps priced above them, such as the 2027 gas swaps at USD 3.91 against USD 2.96. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation calc-norm-margin; calculation calc-hedge; calculation calc-hedge-fv; 10-Q_2026-09-30_inr-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 30–32, 46, 50

Priority is the main structural weakness for the unsecured notes. The USD 875.0 million revolver carries first-priority liens on substantially all assets and is 1.59 times the USD 550.0 million notes; if it were fully drawn, total debt would be USD 1,425.0 million, 3.27x trailing EBITDA, against a leverage test of 3.0x whose definition differs from the one used here, so headroom cannot be calculated. Reported net debt of USD 512.6 million would reach 3.00x if trailing EBITDA fell 60.75%, to USD 170.9 million, so the cushion on reported figures is wide, but the borrowing base, set by lenders at their sole discretion, decides how much of the revolver can be drawn. Basis: calculation calc-fulldraw; calculation calc-cushion; 10-Q_2026-09-30_inr-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 26–28, 47; 10-K_2025-12-31_inr-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 75

Refinancing risk is low until 2028 and then depends on the revolver. The senior notes mature on 2031-04-01, about 4.4 years from the as-of date, carry a fixed coupon, can be redeemed from 2028-04-01, and no other debt principal is due; the revolver's maturity is stated as September 2028 in the 2025 annual report and not restated after the 2026 amendments, about 22 months away if unchanged. An extension depends on a borrowing base that lenders redetermine each spring and autumn, and the autumn 2026 outcome is not in the filings supplied. Basis: calculation calc-tenor; 10-Q_2026-09-30_inr-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 26–28; 10-K_2025-12-31_inr-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 75, 164

The business is larger but concentrated in one basin and a few buyers. Net production rose 88% in the nine months of 2026, and the third-quarter rate was about double that of a year earlier, yet three purchasers took 84% of FY2025 revenue and all production is in Appalachia, where gas prices were weak in the second and third quarters of 2026 on mild weather and higher output. Proved reserves are 67.90% gas by energy content while 48.46% of revenue is oil, so cash flow follows crude prices and reserve value follows gas prices. Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_inr-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 46, 50, 55–56; 10-K_2025-12-31_inr-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 18, 24, 62

Sponsor control and reporting quality add medium governance risk but do not change the credit view on their own. Four sponsors held 68.8% of the voting power at 2026-03-05, the June 2026 amendment widened restricted-payment capacity on terms not supplied, the Series A dividend moved from payment in kind to cash from the second quarter, and five material weaknesses in internal control remain unremediated, which reduces the weight that can be placed on every reported figure. Against that, no Class A dividend, sponsor fee or pre-IPO distribution to owners is reported. Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); Source readiness (CP-0); 10-K_2024-12-31_inr-20241231.htm.jsonl, page 177; 10-K_2025-12-31_inr-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 78, 114; 10-Q_2026-06-30_inr-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 26; 10-Q_2026-09-30_inr-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 38, 72

The primary downside path is a price fall that arrives with a borrowing base cut while fixed charges continue. Lower oil and gas realisations reduce EBITDA and the reserve value behind the base; the lenders can cut the base at their discretion and could require immediate repayment of any excess, while interest, the preferred dividend, firm transportation charges and the spending committed to hold acreage do not fall at the same pace, so liquidity shrinks faster than leverage rises. The levers are slower spending as operator, payment in kind of the preferred dividend until the second anniversary of issue, and the hedges, which cover about two-fifths of 2027 volumes. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_inr-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 27, 37, 43, 47; 10-K_2025-12-31_inr-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 23, 75; calculation calc-hedge

runs.text: Reported leverage and liquidity give room to absorb a price shock. Total debt of USD 538.8 million is 1.24x trailing EBITDA, there is no principal due before 2031-04-01, and USD 901.2 million of cash and undrawn revolver commitments is about 1.92 times trailing capital expenditure, so a spending slowdown would not be forced by a funding gap in the next year. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation calc-liquidity-capex; 10-Q_2026-09-30_inr-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 26–28

Scale and growth support cash flow visibility. Net production rose 88% in nine months 2026 and the third-quarter rate was about double that of a year earlier, EBITDA margin has stayed near two-thirds, and the majority of revenue contracts run longer than twelve months, which gives the cash flow to service USD 69.9 million a year of notes coupon and preferred dividend with room. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation calc-fixed; 10-Q_2026-09-30_inr-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 50, 55–56; 10-K_2025-12-31_inr-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 24

Control of timing gives capital spending flexibility. Infinity operates most of its acreage and the proved development need of about USD 147.4 million a year is well below the USD 470.1 million spent in the last twelve months, so a downturn can be met by slowing the programme, limited by acreage that must be drilled to be held. Basis: calculation calc-capex-need; calculation calc-acreage; 10-K_2025-12-31_inr-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 17, 23, 51; 10-Q_2026-09-30_inr-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 60

Equity-supported funding record lowers the chance of debt-funded distributions. New equity paid for the 2023 acquisition, the IPO proceeds repaid revolver debt, the 2026 acquisition was part-funded with preferred capital and shares, and no pre-IPO distributions were paid, so the record to date has not moved cash to owners ahead of lenders. Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2024-12-31_inr-20241231.htm.jsonl, pages 165, 177; 10-K_2025-12-31_inr-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 15

Maturities are distant and fixed-rate notes limit rate exposure. The notes mature in 2031, carry a fixed coupon and are callable from 2028-04-01, so refinancing is not an issue for about 4.4 years except through the revolver. Basis: calculation calc-tenor; 10-Q_2026-09-30_inr-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 27–28

Cash flow is below spending, so growth relies on outside capital. Free cash flow was negative USD 61.6 million in the last twelve months and USD 107.2 million in FY2025, and financing is expected to keep funding spending, which leaves lenders exposed to the capital market for the next stages of development. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_inr-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 60

The unsecured notes rank behind a larger secured revolver and a preferred stock sits at the parent. The USD 875.0 million revolver is 1.59 times the notes, a full draw would take total debt to 3.27x trailing EBITDA, and the preferred stock adds an 8.0% cumulative claim at the parent, so noteholders' position worsens quickly if the base is used. Basis: calculation calc-fulldraw; calculation calc-fixed; 10-Q_2026-09-30_inr-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 26–28, 37

Price exposure is oil-led in revenue and gas-led in reserves, with only partial hedges. Oil is 48.46% of revenue and gas 67.90% of reserves by energy, hedges cover about 39.98% of oil and 42.63% of gas for 2027, and hedge settlements already cost USD 19.0 million over the last twelve months, so price falls reach cash flow and reserve value at different times. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation calc-hedge; 10-Q_2026-09-30_inr-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 30–31, 55; 10-K_2025-12-31_inr-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 18

Customers are concentrated and production is in one basin. Three purchasers took 84% of FY2025 revenue and all production is in Appalachia, so a dispute, outage or local price weakness at one buyer or pipeline reaches revenue quickly, although the products are fungible. Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_inr-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 24, 62

Governance and reporting quality are weaker than the leverage. Four sponsors held 68.8% of the voting power, the restricted-payment capacity was widened on undisclosed terms and five material weaknesses in internal control are unremediated, which lowers the reliability of every figure and adds a route for cash to leave. Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_inr-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 78; 10-Q_2026-06-30_inr-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 26; 10-Q_2026-09-30_inr-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 72

runs.text: The Antero acquisition closed on 2026-02-23. INR Holdings and Northern Oil and Gas bought upstream assets for about USD 800 million and midstream assets for about USD 400 million at the 100% level, Infinity taking an undivided 60% interest and Northern 40%. Infinity's aggregate cash consideration was USD 681.7 million after the post-closing adjustment process completed on 2026-08-07, down from a preliminary USD 683.9 million; of that, USD 61.2 million was an escrow deposit paid in 2025 and USD 620.5 million was paid in the nine months of 2026. It was funded with cash on hand, the preferred stock proceeds and Credit Facility borrowings. The purchase was accounted for as an asset acquisition, transaction costs reached USD 16.9 million by 2026-09-30, and Infinity operates substantially all of the assets under joint development and cooperation agreements with Northern. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_inr-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 14, 183; 10-Q_2026-03-31_inr-20260331.htm.jsonl, page 19; 10-Q_2026-09-30_inr-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 21–22, 59

The USD 350.0 million Series A convertible preferred stock was sold on 2026-02-23 to affiliates of Quantum (275,000 shares) and Carnelian (75,000 shares) under an agreement signed on 2026-02-18. It carries a cumulative dividend of 8.0% a year for five years and 12.0% after, convertible at USD 21.39 a share, with a Company right to force conversion after three years if the share price holds above 140% of that price and a Company redemption option from the fifth anniversary at a 15.0% annual return. The first quarter's dividend was paid in kind and the second and third quarters in cash. The preferred stock is shown as temporary equity because holders can require repurchase on a change of control; the filings give two net proceeds figures, about USD 337.1 million and about USD 334.0 million. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_inr-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 15, 82; 10-Q_2026-09-30_inr-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 37–38, 48, 61

INR Holdings issued USD 550.0 million of senior notes due 2031 at par on 2026-03-20, guaranteed on a senior unsecured basis by certain subsidiaries, with interest payable each April 1 and October 1 from 2026-10-01 and maturity on 2031-04-01. The notes can be redeemed from 2028-04-01, or earlier with a make-whole premium, and up to 40% can be redeemed with equity proceeds before then; holders can require repurchase at 101% on certain changes of control. The covenants limit debt, restricted payments, asset sales, investments, liens, affiliate transactions and unrestricted subsidiaries. Net proceeds of about USD 537.6 million repaid Credit Facility borrowings, and the coupon and redemption prices are in the transaction register. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_inr-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 27–29, 60

The Credit Facility, led by Citibank, had its commitments and borrowing base raised from USD 375.0 million to USD 875.0 million by the Fourth Amendment on 2026-02-23 and no borrowings were outstanding at 2026-09-30. It is guaranteed by subsidiaries of INR Holdings and secured by first-priority liens on substantially all consolidated assets, with financial tests of a current ratio of at least 1.0x and a total net leverage ratio of no more than 3.0x. The Fifth Amendment on 2026-06-22 expanded the circumstances in which certain restricted payments may be made; the filings do not say which. The facility's maturity is stated only in the 2025 annual report and not after the 2026 amendments. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_inr-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 26–27; 10-Q_2026-06-30_inr-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 26; 10-K_2025-12-31_inr-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 119, 164

The Chase acquisition closed on 2026-01-20 for 2,517,194 Class A shares recorded at USD 35.1 million in equity, adding non-operated Pennsylvania interests in the South Bend Field. The IPO on 2025-02-03 sold 15,237,500 Class A shares at USD 20.00 and its net proceeds repaid USD 285.0 million of Credit Facility borrowings. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_inr-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 15, 182; 10-Q_2026-03-31_inr-20260331.htm.jsonl, page 8

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Source readiness for Infinity Natural Resources, Inc. (inr-2029118), as of 2026-11-18, on the credit snapshot pathway through Fundamental credit. It records which of the five supplied SEC filings can support each requested analysis and what is missing; it makes no credit conclusion.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The five SEC filings support a financial and capital-structure credit snapshot of Infinity Natural Resources, Inc. as of 2026-11-18, but without the financing agreements covenant headroom and creditor protections cannot be confirmed.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Anchor the work on the 2026-09-30 balance sheet: year-end 2025 statements pre-date the Antero acquisition (USD 681.7 million), the Series A preferred issue (USD 350.0 million) and the senior notes issue (USD 550.0 million), so they understate today's capital structure. Management also reports unremediated material weaknesses in internal control, so every reported figure carries a reliability qualification.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The filings give income and cash-flow statements from FY2022 and balance sheets from 2023-12-31 through 2026-09-30, in two annual reports and three 2026 quarterly reports, the latest signed 2026-11-09. Discrete quarters for 2025 and the first three quarters of 2026 and a trailing twelve-month view to 2026-09-30 can be rebuilt from them, but quarterly cash flows must be derived by subtracting year-to-date figures, and no filing reports EBITDA, adjusted EBITDA or free cash flow, so those measures will be constructions rather than reported figures.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The reporting entity changes between the two annual reports. The 2024 annual report carries audited statements of the operating company, Infinity Natural Resources, LLC, known as INR Holdings, while the listed parent presents only nil balance sheets because it had no operations before its February 2025 IPO; from FY2025 the statements consolidate the parent with INR Holdings and show the other owners of INR Holdings as redeemable non-controlling interest. INR Holdings is the borrower under the credit facility and the issuer of the senior notes due 2031, while the Series A preferred stock was issued by the parent, so every debt, cash and leverage figure needs a stated perimeter.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Year-end 2025 statements describe the issuer before the Antero acquisition (closed 2026-02-23 for USD 681.7 million), the Series A preferred issue (USD 350.0 million, 2026-02-23) and the senior notes issue (USD 550.0 million, 2026-03-20). The latest quarterly report states no credit facility borrowings at 2026-09-30 against USD 875.0 million of commitments. The third-quarter report gives pro forma revenue and net income for the acquisition but no pro forma EBITDA or net debt, so any run-rate leverage is an analyst construction and must be labelled as one.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Management reports that disclosure controls were not effective at 2024-12-31, at 2025-12-31 and at each 2026 quarter end because material weaknesses in internal control over financial reporting remained open, including segregation of duties, risk assessment, control activities and formal accounting policies; management reports significant progress toward remediation but gives no completion date. The auditor opined on the statements but not on internal control, so reported figures are usable but carry a reliability qualification that every analysis should carry forward.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: No credit agreement, amendment, indenture, certificate of designation or purchase agreement was supplied, and the run settings declare none, so the filings' summaries are the only evidence of financing terms. The summaries give two maintenance tests, a current ratio of at least 1.0x and a leverage ratio of no more than 3.0x, but no filing reports the ratio or covenant EBITDA, and the 2025 annual report defines leverage as total funded debt to EBITDAX while the second- and third-quarter notes call it a consolidated total net leverage ratio. Covenant headroom is therefore not calculable from this set.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Directors, pay and ownership for FY2025 are incorporated from a proxy statement that is not in the set, so the latest ownership table is as of 2025-03-21. The third-quarter exhibit index lists a transition and severance agreement dated 2026-08-09 with the chief financial officer who signed the first two 2026 quarterly reports, and a different officer signs the third-quarter report; neither the terms nor the successor's appointment are described in the filings supplied. The third-quarter report states no subsequent events, and the set ends 9 days before the as-of date.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The latest reserve estimate is as of 2025-12-31, and the annual report states that its operating information does not give effect to the Antero acquisition unless it says otherwise, so asset coverage for the enlarged asset base is not established.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Financial foundation for Infinity Natural Resources, Inc. (inr-2029118), as of 2026-11-18, on the credit snapshot pathway. It puts the filings' statements on one USD basis, builds the net debt, leverage, cover, liquidity and maturity tables, and logs the gaps and definition conflicts.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Reported leverage is moderate at 1.24x total debt to trailing EBITDA at 2026-09-30 and liquidity is ample, but the EBITDA is constructed and holds the Antero assets for only about seven months, so run-rate leverage is probably lower but is not established.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation calc-ratios-20260930; calculation calc-ltm-ebitda-0930; 10-Q_2026-09-30_inr-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 21

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Total debt is USD 538.8 million of senior notes due 2031 against USD 26.2 million of cash and USD 875.0 million undrawn under the secured facility, with USD 336.5 million of Series A preferred stock and USD 706.3 million of redeemable non-controlling interest outside total debt. Free cash flow was negative at USD 61.6 million over the trailing twelve months, and the 54.51x cash interest cover is overstated because the first note coupon was payable after the quarter end.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_inr-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 7–8, 11, 27, 38; calculation calc-fcf; calculation calc-ratios-20260930

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Total debt to EBITDA moved from 1.55x at 2024-12-31 to 1.30x at 2025-12-31 and 1.24x at 2026-09-30, but the three readings describe different companies: year-end 2025 debt of USD 150.9 million was revolver borrowings before the Antero acquisition, while the latest USD 538.8 million is the 2031 notes after it. The trailing EBITDA of USD 435.4 million no longer carries the one-time IPO share-based charge that depressed FY2025 and holds Antero only from 2026-02-23, so a full-period ratio would probably be lower, but no filing states pro forma EBITDA and the amount is not established. Net debt to EBITDA is 1.18x.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation calc-ltm-ebitda-0930; calculation calc-ratios-20260930; 10-K_2025-12-31_inr-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 144–145; 10-Q_2026-09-30_inr-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 7–9, 21–22

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Cash interest cover of 54.51x says little about capacity: cash interest paid over the trailing twelve months was only USD 8.0 million because the first coupon on the 2031 notes was payable on 2026-10-01, so the denominator omits the interest the notes now carry. EBITDA to net interest expense on the accrual basis is 11.78x and is the better indicator, although it too includes the notes only from their March 2026 issue date.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation calc-ltm-interest-0930; calculation calc-ltm-interest-net-0930; 10-Q_2026-09-30_inr-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 8, 27, 43

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Operating cash flow of USD 408.6 million over the trailing twelve months fell short of capital expenditure of USD 470.1 million, so free cash flow was negative at USD 61.6 million before the USD 620.5 million paid for Antero, and capital expenditure ran at 103.52% of revenue in FY2025 and 72.68% in the nine months of 2026. The gap is financed with debt and preferred stock, so leverage rises unless capital spending slows or EBITDA catches up; the issuer states that it operates the vast majority of its acreage and can defer or accelerate part of its programme, which is the main mitigant. Cash settlements on hedges turned from an inflow of USD 12.2 million in FY2025 to a net outflow of USD 19.0 million over the trailing twelve months; they sit below operating income, so EBITDA excludes them while operating cash flow carries them. Working capital was a modest inflow, mostly from royalties payable, which more than doubled over the nine months partly through royalties assumed with Antero, and from trade payables; these are interest-free balances that reverse if payment timing normalises, so part of the cash flow is timing.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation calc-fcf; calculation calc-capex; calculation calc-ltm-hedge-0930; 10-K_2025-12-31_inr-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 146; 10-Q_2026-09-30_inr-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 11, 60

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Liquidity is USD 901.2 million, being USD 26.2 million of cash plus USD 875.0 million undrawn, and the maturity ladder drawn from the filings shows no principal due before the 2031 notes, so near-term refinancing risk is low on the figures. The commitment is only as firm as the borrowing base, which is redetermined twice a year against reserve values, and the filings do not restate the facility maturity after the 2026 amendments (the 2025 annual report gives September 2028); the credit agreement that would settle both points is not in the set.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation calc-liquidity; calculation calc-ladder; 10-Q_2026-09-30_inr-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 26–27; 10-K_2025-12-31_inr-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 164

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Two claims sit between liabilities and equity and are outside total debt: USD 336.5 million of Series A preferred stock, which carries an 8.0% cumulative dividend paid in cash since the second quarter and ranks ahead of the common stock, and USD 706.3 million of redeemable non-controlling interest held by the other owners of INR Holdings. Neither is a creditor claim, but the preferred dividend is a fixed cash draw ahead of equity and a change of control gives its holders a put, so the leverage ratios understate the fixed claims on cash flow. Operating leases are small and sit on their own balance sheet lines outside debt; the firm transportation and drilling rig commitments are disclosed in the notes but are not in any figure here.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Three data issues limit how far the figures can be pushed. Management reports unremediated material weaknesses in internal control, so every reported line carries a reliability qualification. Small differences stay unexplained in the filings, such as a USD 24 thousand gap in nine-month 2026 depreciation, depletion, and amortization between the income statement and the cash flow statement and USD 1 thousand of rounding in quarterly sums, none of which moves a ratio at two decimals. And the definitions differ from the covenant: EBITDA here is operating income plus depreciation, depletion, and amortization, while the facility tests total funded debt to a consolidated EBITDAX, or a net leverage ratio, defined in a document that is not supplied, so covenant headroom is not calculable.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The reporting perimeter changes in FY2025: FY2023 and FY2024 are the operating company's own results, audited in the 2024 annual report and carried as comparatives in the 2025 annual report, while FY2025 onward consolidate the listed parent, so the fiscal-year ratios share an operating business but not an owner structure. No subsequent event after 2026-09-30 changes net debt in the sources read, and the 2025-12-31 net debt of USD 148.0 million should not be quoted as a current figure because the Antero acquisition, the preferred issue and the notes issue all followed it.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Subsequent events: the third-quarter report states no subsequent event requiring recognition or disclosure and is dated 2026-11-09; the 2025 annual report flags the Chase Acquisition of 2026-01-20, the Antero Acquisition of 2026-02-23 and the Series A Preferred Stock issue of 2026-02-23, all of which are in the 2026 quarterly balance sheets and are not blended into the FY2025 column.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Total debt and net debt are balance sheet carrying values over reported EBITDA calculated from operating income plus depreciation, depletion, and amortization, and the interim rows use last-twelve-months EBITDA that holds the Antero assets from 2026-02-23 only.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The interim figures divide EBITDA by cash interest paid, which omits the first coupon on the senior notes payable on 2026-10-01, so they overstate cover.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Undrawn committed facilities are the capacity the filings state, which depends on a borrowing base that is redetermined semi-annually.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The ladder is contractual principal at 2026-09-30; the facility has no borrowings, so only the senior notes due 2031 appear.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: EBITDA is reported EBITDA calculated from operating income plus depreciation, depletion, and amortization, and the FY2025 figure carries a one-time IPO share-based charge.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Cumulative leverage is on principal over last-twelve-months EBITDA, which holds the Antero assets from 2026-02-23 only.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: No bridge is stated because the issuer reports no adjusted EBITDA.

fields.name: Quote

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: High: the issuer states no pro forma or full-period EBITDA for the Antero assets, so leverage and cover at 2026-03-31, 2026-06-30 and 2026-09-30 are last-twelve-months figures that hold the acquired assets from 2026-02-23 only and run-rate leverage is not established. A lender presentation or the issuer's own pro forma EBITDA would close it.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: High: the issuer reports no EBITDA or adjusted EBITDA, so EBITDA is calculated from operating income plus depreciation, depletion, and amortization and the covenant EBITDAX cannot be reproduced; covenant headroom is not calculable. The credit agreement would close it.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Medium: cash interest paid over the last twelve months omits the first coupon on the senior notes due 2031, payable on 2026-10-01, so cash interest cover at 2026-03-31, 2026-06-30 and 2026-09-30 is not a measure of capacity. Interest paid for the fourth quarter of 2026 would close it.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Medium: the facility maturity is stated only in the 2025 annual report (September 2028) and not after the 2026 amendments, so the maturity ladder shows nothing maturing for an undrawn facility whose term is unconfirmed. The credit agreement would close it.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Medium: the issuer states no adjusted EBITDA or add-backs, so the EBITDA bridge is not supplied; the one-time IPO share-based compensation of USD 126.1 million is shown in general and administrative expense but is not added back. An issuer-stated adjusted figure would close it.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Medium: the statements print no segment split because the company has one reportable segment, and no cost of sales or gross profit because costs are shown by nature, so no segment schedule is written. The issuer's split of capital expenditure between maintenance and growth, and cash taxes paid in 2026, are not stated either; the annual reports state that no entity-level income taxes were paid for FY2023 to FY2025.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Low: cells shown as a dash in the filings are recorded as not supplied rather than zero. They are income tax, share-based compensation and deferred income taxes for FY2023 and FY2024; the Antero, escrow deposit, Series A, notes, dividend and other financing lines in the periods where they do not appear; and balance sheet lines such as the short-term deposit on acquisitions, the deferred tax lines and the mezzanine lines at 2024-12-31. No amount is assumed, and each statement's printed totals still add up.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Low: the midstream operations and maintenance expense line is printed only in the 2026 reports and their 2025 comparatives, so the annual columns show it as not supplied; EBITDA and total operating expenses are unaffected.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Low: depreciation, depletion, and amortization differs between the income statement and the cash flow statement by USD 24 thousand for nine months 2026 and by USD 18 thousand for six months 2025, and the filings do not explain it. Both figures are kept and EBITDA uses the income statement.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Low: the FY2024 balance sheet follows the 2025 annual report, which shows credit facility borrowings of USD 259.406 million; the 2024 annual report shows a line of credit of USD 259.347 million plus notes payable of USD 0.160 million, which is USD 259.507 million on that presentation. Totals of assets and liabilities are unchanged.

fields.name: Quote

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Low: debt, cash and leverage are on the consolidated perimeter of INR Holdings and its subsidiaries; the filings give no separate statements or guarantor financial information for the notes' guarantor group, so guarantor and non-guarantor cash flows are not separable.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Business and governance fact base for Infinity Natural Resources, Inc. (inr-2029118), as of 2026-11-18, on the credit snapshot pathway. It covers what the company does, who owns and controls it, the 2026 transactions and the governance and sponsor evidence in the five filings supplied, and makes no recommendation on any instrument.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Business risk is moderate and governance risk is medium: Infinity is a larger Appalachian producer after the Antero purchase, but four sponsors held 68.8% of the voting power at 2026-03-05 and the documents showing creditor protection were not supplied, so protection is unverified. Operating evidence is solid, with nine-month 2026 net production up 88%, so the creditor risk lies in structure rather than operations.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The notes are issued by INR Holdings, of which the listed parent owns 31.8%, and USD 350.0 million of 8.0% cumulative preferred stock now ranks ahead of the common equity at the parent. The filings supplied document no sponsor extraction, but material weaknesses in internal control are not reported as remediated.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Operating scale has stepped up, and revenue leans toward oil while reserves lean toward gas. Net production for the nine months of 2026 rose 88%, and oil supplied 48.46% of revenue against 33.91% for natural gas and 16.23% for NGLs, yet proved reserves at 2025-12-31 were 67.90% natural gas by energy content. The reserve value behind the borrowing base is therefore likely to be more sensitive to gas prices than current cash flow is, which follows oil prices; the filings do not split reserve value by product, so this is an interpretation and not a measurement.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation calc-mix-9m26; calculation calc-reserve-mix; 10-Q_2026-09-30_inr-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 55–56; 10-K_2025-12-31_inr-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 17–18

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Customer concentration is high, although the products are fungible. Three purchasers took 84% of net revenue in FY2025 (BP America 35%, Marathon Oil 33% and Ergon 16%) and owed 95% of oil and gas sales receivables at year-end, and the 2026 reports say three customers exceeded 10% of revenue without naming them. Management states that losing any one purchaser would not materially affect results because crude oil and natural gas have established markets; that is management's view, and the filings give no contract terms to test it.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The Antero acquisition is the largest change to the credit, and reported figures show only part of its effect. Infinity paid USD 681.7 million for a 60% undivided interest in upstream and midstream assets in Ohio, funded by USD 334.0 million of net preferred proceeds and revolver borrowings that the notes later refinanced, and the assets added USD 72.0 million of revenue from 2026-02-23. Assuming ownership from 2025-01-01, nine-month revenue grew 65.41% rather than the 118.69% reported, so reported growth overstates the underlying rate. The filings give no pro forma EBITDA, no reserves net to Infinity for the acquired assets and no itemised bridge from the USD 720.0 million that 60% of the headline price implies to the USD 681.7 million paid.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation calc-antero; calculation calc-pf-growth; 10-Q_2026-09-30_inr-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 21–22, 48, 61; 10-Q_2026-03-31_inr-20260331.htm.jsonl, page 19; 10-K_2025-12-31_inr-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 14, 183

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Creditors face a holding-company structure with a preferred claim above the common equity. INR Holdings is the borrower and notes issuer, the listed parent owns 31.8% of it and the Legacy Owners hold 68.2% as exchangeable units. The notes are senior unsecured, rank equally with the Credit Facility in right of payment, sit effectively behind its first-priority liens on substantially all assets and structurally behind any future subsidiary that does not guarantee them; the filings do not name the current guarantors or say that the parent guarantees either debt. The USD 350.0 million Series A preferred stock sits at the parent and carries an 8.0% cumulative dividend, about USD 28.0 million a year, which the parent can pay only from distributions that the credit agreement restricts and that a June 2026 amendment widened.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Control is concentrated with four financial sponsors, so any change of control is a decision for a few holders. Pearl, NGP, Quantum and Carnelian held 68.8% of the voting power at 2026-03-05 (36.2%, 12.1%, 16.1% and 4.4%), Pearl may nominate four directors, Carnelian appoints one and NGP's right to nominate one is unused; the filings describe them as acting separately. Series A holders also hold consent rights over dividends, over debt above a threshold the filings do not state and over deviations from set hedging requirements. Three change-of-control terms stack: the notes carry a 101% repurchase right, the preferred holders can require repurchase at the greater of a 13.0% annual return and 1.30x the initial USD 350.0 million, and the tax receivable agreement accelerates, with payments to the Legacy Owners estimated at approximately USD 134.3 million at 2025-02-03.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation calc-votes; 10-K_2025-12-31_inr-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 78, 82; 10-Q_2026-09-30_inr-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 28, 37–38; 10-K_2024-12-31_inr-20241231.htm.jsonl, pages 214, 216

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Documented behaviour to date adds to the equity base rather than removing cash, with three items to watch. INR Holdings raised USD 222.3 million of new Class B equity for the 2023 Ohio Utica purchase from an owner group that was 98.1% Pearl and NGP affiliates at the 2024 year-end and paid no distributions to members in 2023 or 2024, the IPO's USD 286.5 million of net proceeds repaid USD 285.0 million of revolver debt, Quantum and Carnelian put USD 350.0 million of new capital into the preferred stock in 2026 and the Chase acquisition was paid in shares. The items to watch are the Series A dividend moving from payment in kind to cash from the second quarter (USD 14.1 million paid for two quarters), the June 2026 widening of restricted-payment capacity, and a USD 75.0 million repurchase program with USD 72.3 million unused at 2026-06-30. No dividend on the Class A common stock and no sponsor fee is reported in the filings supplied, but the FY2025 related-party disclosure sits in a proxy statement that was not supplied.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Reporting quality is the weakest governance evidence and limits how far any figure can be relied on. Management concluded that disclosure controls were not effective at each reporting date from 2024-12-31 to 2026-09-30 because five material weaknesses (segregation of duties, risk assessment, control activities, formal accounting policies and accounting resources) are not reported as remediated, and the auditor need not attest to internal control until the company ceases to be an emerging growth company, which could be as late as the FY2030 annual report. The chief financial officer who signed the first two 2026 quarterly reports entered a transition and severance agreement dated 2026-08-09 and a different officer signed the third quarterly report; the filings give no terms and no successor details beyond the signature.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The strongest evidence against a medium rating is the record so far: new equity was raised in 2023 and no distributions were paid to members in 2023 or 2024, the IPO proceeds repaid revolver debt, the 2026 acquisitions were funded with new preferred capital, shares and notes that refinanced the revolver, no Class A dividend is reported, and the revolver was undrawn at 2026-09-30 with USD 875.0 million of capacity. Sponsor board rights also fall with ownership: Pearl's voting power was 36.2% at 2026-03-05 against 47.5% of Class A and Class B votes at 2025-03-21, although the two measures use different bases. The view would improve to low if the financing documents confirmed tight restricted-payment and debt limits with full guarantee coverage, the weaknesses in internal control were reported as remediated and the FY2025 proxy statement showed a majority of independent directors. It would worsen to high if the widened restricted-payment capacity were used for a common dividend, a sponsor fee or buybacks while borrowings rose, if the 2.0% a year step-up on the Series A dividend applied because the credit agreement blocked cash payment, or if a change of control triggered the preferred repurchase and the tax receivable acceleration together.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The credit agreement, indenture, certificate of designation and Antero purchase agreements were not supplied, so the medium governance rating rests on the filings' summaries of restricted-payment, debt and guarantee terms, and reading the documents could move it either way.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The FY2025 proxy statement was not supplied, so board size, independence, committee membership and related-party dealings after 2025-03-21 are not established, and the control conclusion rests on the 2026-03-05 voting figures alone.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - No pro forma EBITDA, net reserves or integration targets are stated for the Antero assets, so the view that the acquisition is manageable cannot be tested and the transaction conclusion uses pro forma revenue only.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Sponsor fund vintage, remaining fund life, entry values and sponsor economics are not disclosed, so no conclusion is drawn about sponsor exit timing or selling pressure.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The 2026 customer names and shares are not given, so the concentration finding rests on FY2025 and may not hold for the enlarged company.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The Antero acquisition closed on 2026-02-23. INR Holdings and Northern Oil and Gas bought upstream assets for about USD 800 million and midstream assets for about USD 400 million at the 100% level, Infinity taking an undivided 60% interest and Northern 40%. Infinity's aggregate cash consideration was USD 681.7 million after the post-closing adjustment process completed on 2026-08-07, down from a preliminary USD 683.9 million; of that, USD 61.2 million was an escrow deposit paid in 2025 and USD 620.5 million was paid in the nine months of 2026. It was funded with cash on hand, the preferred stock proceeds and Credit Facility borrowings. The purchase was accounted for as an asset acquisition, transaction costs reached USD 16.9 million by 2026-09-30, and Infinity operates substantially all of the assets under joint development and cooperation agreements with Northern.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The USD 350.0 million Series A convertible preferred stock was sold on 2026-02-23 to affiliates of Quantum (275,000 shares) and Carnelian (75,000 shares) under an agreement signed on 2026-02-18. It carries a cumulative dividend of 8.0% a year for five years and 12.0% after, convertible at USD 21.39 a share, with a Company right to force conversion after three years if the share price holds above 140% of that price and a Company redemption option from the fifth anniversary at a 15.0% annual return. The first quarter's dividend was paid in kind and the second and third quarters in cash. The preferred stock is shown as temporary equity because holders can require repurchase on a change of control; the filings give two net proceeds figures, about USD 337.1 million and about USD 334.0 million.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: INR Holdings issued USD 550.0 million of senior notes due 2031 at par on 2026-03-20, guaranteed on a senior unsecured basis by certain subsidiaries, with interest payable each April 1 and October 1 from 2026-10-01 and maturity on 2031-04-01. The notes can be redeemed from 2028-04-01, or earlier with a make-whole premium, and up to 40% can be redeemed with equity proceeds before then; holders can require repurchase at 101% on certain changes of control. The covenants limit debt, restricted payments, asset sales, investments, liens, affiliate transactions and unrestricted subsidiaries. Net proceeds of about USD 537.6 million repaid Credit Facility borrowings, and the coupon and redemption prices are in the transaction register.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The Credit Facility, led by Citibank, had its commitments and borrowing base raised from USD 375.0 million to USD 875.0 million by the Fourth Amendment on 2026-02-23 and no borrowings were outstanding at 2026-09-30. It is guaranteed by subsidiaries of INR Holdings and secured by first-priority liens on substantially all consolidated assets, with financial tests of a current ratio of at least 1.0x and a total net leverage ratio of no more than 3.0x. The Fifth Amendment on 2026-06-22 expanded the circumstances in which certain restricted payments may be made; the filings do not say which. The facility's maturity is stated only in the 2025 annual report and not after the 2026 amendments.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The Chase acquisition closed on 2026-01-20 for 2,517,194 Class A shares recorded at USD 35.1 million in equity, adding non-operated Pennsylvania interests in the South Bend Field. The IPO on 2025-02-03 sold 15,237,500 Class A shares at USD 20.00 and its net proceeds repaid USD 285.0 million of Credit Facility borrowings.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Module status: Ready with Limitations. The five filings are primary documents; the financing agreements and the FY2025 proxy statement are not among them.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Sponsor / Governance Risk Level: Medium. The level is driven by concentrated sponsor control, a cash-pay preferred claim and a widened restricted-payment capacity, because these can move cash or decisions to equity ahead of creditors, which implies a monitoring posture rather than a negative view. Countervailing evidence is documented equity support and repayment of revolver debt with equity.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Fundamental credit assessment for Infinity Natural Resources, Inc. (inr-2029118), as of 2026-11-18, on the credit snapshot pathway. It combines the source readiness, financial and business and governance work into one credit view, a materiality ranking and monitoring triggers; it assigns no rating and makes no security recommendation.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Fundamental credit quality is adequate: reported leverage of 1.24x and USD 901.2 million of liquidity are comfortable, but operating cash flow does not fund growth spending, so unsecured noteholders rely on spending discipline and on a revolver that ranks ahead of them. Free cash flow was negative USD 61.6 million over the last twelve months, three purchasers take most revenue, and the primary downside is a commodity price fall that cuts the borrowing base while interest, preferred dividends and transport charges continue.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_inr-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 26–28, 60

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Governance risk is medium, as the earlier business and governance work found, and no drawn debt principal falls due before the notes mature in 2031.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Reported leverage is low and liquidity is large, but the debt figure leaves out claims that sit beside it. Total debt was USD 538.8 million at 2026-09-30 against trailing EBITDA of USD 435.4 million, 1.24x, or 1.18x net of USD 26.2 million of cash; adding the USD 336.5 million Series A preferred stock at carrying value lifts the ratio to 2.01x, and the USD 706.3 million of redeemable non-controlling interest is the Legacy Owners' claim on the same assets. The issuer reports no EBITDA, so it is operating income plus depreciation, depletion and amortization; it includes the Antero assets only from 2026-02-23 and leaves out USD 19.0 million of net derivative settlement losses over the period. Liquidity of USD 901.2 million is cash plus an undrawn revolver whose size is set by a borrowing base that lenders redetermine twice a year.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation calc-adj-lev; 10-K_2025-12-31_inr-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 75; 10-Q_2026-09-30_inr-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 26–27

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Cash generation does not yet cover the growth programme, which is the central weakness. Operating cash flow of USD 408.6 million over the last twelve months fell short of capital expenditure of USD 470.1 million, leaving free cash flow of negative USD 61.6 million before the USD 620.5 million paid for Antero, and management expects financing to keep funding spending through the rest of 2026. About USD 41.9 million a year of coupon on the notes and USD 28.0 million of cash preferred dividends now come before debt reduction. A large part of the spending looks discretionary: developing the proved undeveloped and non-producing reserves needs about USD 737 million over five years, or USD 147.4 million a year, against USD 470.1 million spent, although that figure excludes Antero, midstream and land and 23.23% of undeveloped acreage expires by 2030, which holds some drilling in place.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation calc-fixed; calculation calc-capex-need; calculation calc-acreage; 10-K_2025-12-31_inr-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 23, 51; 10-Q_2026-09-30_inr-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 27, 37, 60

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Margins are high and have held through price swings, but they rest on prices the company does not control. EBITDA was 67.97% of revenue over the last twelve months and 66.82% in the first nine months of 2026, against 65.84% in FY2023 and 64.65% in FY2024; FY2025 shows 32.45% because of USD 126.1 million of one-off non-cash IPO share compensation, and 67.82% without it, which is a normalisation by this analysis. Oil supplied 48.46% of nine-month revenue and gas and NGLs 50.14%, and the 2027 hedges cover roughly 39.98% of annualised third-quarter oil volume and 42.63% of gas volume; the hedge book was a net liability of USD 23.1 million, because oil and NGL swaps priced below current benchmarks, such as the 2027 oil swaps at USD 65.08 a barrel against USD 87.22 in the third quarter, outweigh gains on gas swaps priced above them, such as the 2027 gas swaps at USD 3.91 against USD 2.96.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation calc-norm-margin; calculation calc-hedge; calculation calc-hedge-fv; 10-Q_2026-09-30_inr-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 30–32, 46, 50

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Priority is the main structural weakness for the unsecured notes. The USD 875.0 million revolver carries first-priority liens on substantially all assets and is 1.59 times the USD 550.0 million notes; if it were fully drawn, total debt would be USD 1,425.0 million, 3.27x trailing EBITDA, against a leverage test of 3.0x whose definition differs from the one used here, so headroom cannot be calculated. Reported net debt of USD 512.6 million would reach 3.00x if trailing EBITDA fell 60.75%, to USD 170.9 million, so the cushion on reported figures is wide, but the borrowing base, set by lenders at their sole discretion, decides how much of the revolver can be drawn.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation calc-fulldraw; calculation calc-cushion; 10-Q_2026-09-30_inr-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 26–28, 47; 10-K_2025-12-31_inr-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 75

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Refinancing risk is low until 2028 and then depends on the revolver. The senior notes mature on 2031-04-01, about 4.4 years from the as-of date, carry a fixed coupon, can be redeemed from 2028-04-01, and no other debt principal is due; the revolver's maturity is stated as September 2028 in the 2025 annual report and not restated after the 2026 amendments, about 22 months away if unchanged. An extension depends on a borrowing base that lenders redetermine each spring and autumn, and the autumn 2026 outcome is not in the filings supplied.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The business is larger but concentrated in one basin and a few buyers. Net production rose 88% in the nine months of 2026, and the third-quarter rate was about double that of a year earlier, yet three purchasers took 84% of FY2025 revenue and all production is in Appalachia, where gas prices were weak in the second and third quarters of 2026 on mild weather and higher output. Proved reserves are 67.90% gas by energy content while 48.46% of revenue is oil, so cash flow follows crude prices and reserve value follows gas prices.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Sponsor control and reporting quality add medium governance risk but do not change the credit view on their own. Four sponsors held 68.8% of the voting power at 2026-03-05, the June 2026 amendment widened restricted-payment capacity on terms not supplied, the Series A dividend moved from payment in kind to cash from the second quarter, and five material weaknesses in internal control remain unremediated, which reduces the weight that can be placed on every reported figure. Against that, no Class A dividend, sponsor fee or pre-IPO distribution to owners is reported.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); Source readiness (CP-0); 10-K_2024-12-31_inr-20241231.htm.jsonl, page 177; 10-K_2025-12-31_inr-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 78, 114; 10-Q_2026-06-30_inr-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 26; 10-Q_2026-09-30_inr-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 38, 72

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The primary downside path is a price fall that arrives with a borrowing base cut while fixed charges continue. Lower oil and gas realisations reduce EBITDA and the reserve value behind the base; the lenders can cut the base at their discretion and could require immediate repayment of any excess, while interest, the preferred dividend, firm transportation charges and the spending committed to hold acreage do not fall at the same pace, so liquidity shrinks faster than leverage rises. The levers are slower spending as operator, payment in kind of the preferred dividend until the second anniversary of issue, and the hedges, which cover about two-fifths of 2027 volumes.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The strongest evidence for a better view is balance sheet strength and margin: reported leverage of 1.24x, USD 901.2 million of liquidity, an undrawn revolver, EBITDA margins near two-thirds, no principal due for more than four years and spending that is largely at management's discretion, with run-rate fixed charges of USD 74.3 million covered 5.86x by trailing EBITDA. It would earn a stronger view if free cash flow turned positive with spending held near the development need of the proved reserves, the autumn borrowing base held at USD 875.0 million, the facility maturity were extended, and the material weaknesses were reported as remediated. The view would weaken if the borrowing base were cut while prices fell, if free cash flow stayed negative into 2027 with the preferred dividend paid in cash, if the widened restricted-payment capacity were used for payments to equity, or if run-rate earnings for the Antero assets proved lower than the trailing figures imply.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation calc-fixed; calculation calc-capex-need; 10-Q_2026-09-30_inr-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 26–27, 37

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Antero earnings enter the trailing figures only from 2026-02-23 and no pro forma EBITDA is stated, so the leverage and cover conclusions rest on a partial period and the true run-rate could be higher or lower.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - No rating, market price or peer set was supplied, so the view of adequate credit quality is an absolute judgement and the comparison with typical issuers in the sector is not established.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The autumn 2026 borrowing base outcome and the amended facility maturity are not in the filings, so the liquidity and refinancing conclusions rest on the 2026-09-30 commitments of USD 875.0 million and could change after the redetermination.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Hedge cover is measured against annualised third-quarter production and mixes hedged MMBtu with produced Mcf, so the coverage shares are approximate and the downside levers are sized only roughly.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Reserves and their value are at 2025-12-31 on SEC prices and exclude the Antero assets, so asset coverage of the enlarged debt is not established and the downside is qualitative, not a forecast.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Reported leverage and liquidity give room to absorb a price shock. Total debt of USD 538.8 million is 1.24x trailing EBITDA, there is no principal due before 2031-04-01, and USD 901.2 million of cash and undrawn revolver commitments is about 1.92 times trailing capital expenditure, so a spending slowdown would not be forced by a funding gap in the next year.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation calc-liquidity-capex; 10-Q_2026-09-30_inr-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 26–28

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Scale and growth support cash flow visibility. Net production rose 88% in nine months 2026 and the third-quarter rate was about double that of a year earlier, EBITDA margin has stayed near two-thirds, and the majority of revenue contracts run longer than twelve months, which gives the cash flow to service USD 69.9 million a year of notes coupon and preferred dividend with room.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation calc-fixed; 10-Q_2026-09-30_inr-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 50, 55–56; 10-K_2025-12-31_inr-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 24

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Control of timing gives capital spending flexibility. Infinity operates most of its acreage and the proved development need of about USD 147.4 million a year is well below the USD 470.1 million spent in the last twelve months, so a downturn can be met by slowing the programme, limited by acreage that must be drilled to be held.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation calc-capex-need; calculation calc-acreage; 10-K_2025-12-31_inr-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 17, 23, 51; 10-Q_2026-09-30_inr-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 60

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Equity-supported funding record lowers the chance of debt-funded distributions. New equity paid for the 2023 acquisition, the IPO proceeds repaid revolver debt, the 2026 acquisition was part-funded with preferred capital and shares, and no pre-IPO distributions were paid, so the record to date has not moved cash to owners ahead of lenders.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Maturities are distant and fixed-rate notes limit rate exposure. The notes mature in 2031, carry a fixed coupon and are callable from 2028-04-01, so refinancing is not an issue for about 4.4 years except through the revolver.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Cash flow is below spending, so growth relies on outside capital. Free cash flow was negative USD 61.6 million in the last twelve months and USD 107.2 million in FY2025, and financing is expected to keep funding spending, which leaves lenders exposed to the capital market for the next stages of development.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The unsecured notes rank behind a larger secured revolver and a preferred stock sits at the parent. The USD 875.0 million revolver is 1.59 times the notes, a full draw would take total debt to 3.27x trailing EBITDA, and the preferred stock adds an 8.0% cumulative claim at the parent, so noteholders' position worsens quickly if the base is used.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation calc-fulldraw; calculation calc-fixed; 10-Q_2026-09-30_inr-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 26–28, 37

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Price exposure is oil-led in revenue and gas-led in reserves, with only partial hedges. Oil is 48.46% of revenue and gas 67.90% of reserves by energy, hedges cover about 39.98% of oil and 42.63% of gas for 2027, and hedge settlements already cost USD 19.0 million over the last twelve months, so price falls reach cash flow and reserve value at different times.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation calc-hedge; 10-Q_2026-09-30_inr-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 30–31, 55; 10-K_2025-12-31_inr-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 18

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Customers are concentrated and production is in one basin. Three purchasers took 84% of FY2025 revenue and all production is in Appalachia, so a dispute, outage or local price weakness at one buyer or pipeline reaches revenue quickly, although the products are fungible.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Governance and reporting quality are weaker than the leverage. Four sponsors held 68.8% of the voting power, the restricted-payment capacity was widened on undisclosed terms and five material weaknesses in internal control are unremediated, which lowers the reliability of every figure and adds a route for cash to leave.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_inr-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 78; 10-Q_2026-06-30_inr-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 26; 10-Q_2026-09-30_inr-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 72

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Infinity is an Appalachian oil, gas and NGL producer that owns gathering and water assets, and it reached its present scale through the 2026 Antero purchase. The listed parent owns 31.8% of INR Holdings, which is the borrower and the notes issuer, so creditors lend to a subsidiary of a holding company whose preferred stock and sponsor holders sit above and beside the debt. This matters for credit because cash can reach the parent and its preferred holders only through distributions that the credit agreement restricts and that a June 2026 amendment widened; it supports cash flow visibility through scale but weakens the clarity of who is paid first.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Ownership and control are concentrated: Pearl, NGP, Quantum and Carnelian held 68.8% of the voting power at 2026-03-05, Pearl nominates four directors, the preferred holders hold consent rights over dividends, debt above an unstated threshold and hedging, and there are three stacked change-of-control claims. This gives stability of strategy and an event risk at a sale, and the documents that would show limits on payments to equity and guarantees were not supplied, so willingness to extract cash is not inferred from identity.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Revenue is cyclical and price-taking rather than contracted: oil, gas and NGL sales are priced off market indices with differentials, most contracts last longer than twelve months, and the mix is oil-led while reserves are gas-led, so the revenue stream does not carry the visibility of contracted income. Three purchasers took 84% of FY2025 revenue, the company states that losing one would not be material, and growth has come from drilling and Antero rather than price. The credit consequence is that debt service capacity moves with prices and that concentration is a monitoring point, not a loss estimate.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Costs are mostly volume-linked with fixed elements that are growing. Per-unit lease operating cost was USD 2.07 per Boe and gathering, processing and transport cost USD 4.25 per Boe in FY2025, direct operating expenses rose to USD 1.28 per Mcfe in nine months 2026 from USD 1.23, and firm transportation added about USD 0.15 per Mcfe in the third quarter, a fixed charge that applies whatever the volumes. Margins can be defended against modest price falls through the low cash cost base, but the fixed transport charge, interest and preferred dividend lift operating leverage if volumes or differentials disappoint.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Capital intensity is high: capital expenditure was 103.52% of revenue in FY2025 and 72.68% in nine months 2026, and operating cash flow covered 86.90% of capital expenditure over the last twelve months. EBITDA converts to free cash flow only after growth spending is cut, so durable cash for debt reduction depends on moving from development of new locations toward the proved development need and on the roughly USD 147.4 million a year that development requires.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation calc-capex-need; calculation calc-ocf-capex; 10-K_2025-12-31_inr-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 51

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Rivalry is intense for acreage, services and capital, and larger competitors can pay more, which limits Infinity's ability to add inventory on good terms. Buyer power is concentrated in three customers but softened by fungible products; supplier power shows in rig, crew and service costs and in transport pipelines the company does not control, which can raise cost or interrupt sales. The threat of new entrants is low where acreage is held by production, with roughly 82% of Ohio acreage held, and substitutes matter mainly through gas competing with other fuels and through energy-transition policy. For credit, rivalry and supplier cost raise the cost of growth and transport constrains realisations rather than creating default risk by themselves.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Political, regulatory and economic factors are material: hydraulic fracturing and water rules, climate policy, oil prices that ranged from USD 60.04 to USD 102.13 a barrel in 2026 amid geopolitical conflict, inflation in service costs and floating-rate borrowing costs with no interest rate hedge all reach margins, spending and liquidity. Social and technological factors do not appear to be a primary credit driver on the materials provided. The credit consequence is volatility in cash flow and in the borrowing base rather than a structural impairment.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Credit-translated strengths are scale, margin, liquidity, distant maturities and operator control; weaknesses are negative free cash flow, notes behind the revolver, concentrated customers and governance; opportunities are the integration of Antero assets and midstream control that could lower costs, as management says, and threats are a lower gas price, a smaller borrowing base and use of widened restricted-payment capacity.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The nine dimensions of the financial profile resolve as follows. Scale and market position is average, because production has nearly doubled but the company is single-basin with a small workforce. Competitive advantage is average, resting on contiguous acreage, owned midstream and operator control rather than contracts. Business diversification is weak, with one basin, three buyers and oil-and-gas-price exposure. Cost and capex flexibility is average, because the development-need gap allows cuts but acreage that must be drilled sets a floor. Margin stability is average, with margins near two-thirds that depend on prices. Free cash flow stability is weak, at negative USD 61.6 million trailing. Ability to refinance is average, helped by distant maturities and an undrawn revolver but dependent on the borrowing base and on market access, which the USD 550.0 million notes issue of March 2026 shows was open then. Liquidity position is strong at USD 901.2 million, subject to the base. Financial policy and governance is average, with sponsor control, preferred claims and unremediated control weaknesses offset by an equity-supported record.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation calc-capex-need; 10-Q_2026-09-30_inr-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 26–28

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Over the next 12 to 24 months the third-quarter production rate of 431.7 MMcfe per day, the first two full quarters of Antero ownership and 2027 hedges at USD 65.08 for oil and USD 3.91 for gas support cash flow, while headwinds are weak gas prices, hedge losses on oil, preferred dividends in cash, the autumn base redetermination and a facility maturity in September 2028 if not extended. Over three to five years the proved development need of about USD 737 million, a call date for the notes on 2028-04-01 and a 2031-04-01 maturity define the refinancing window; whether free cash flow turns positive depends on spending, not on the notes.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation calc-capex-need; calculation calc-tenor; 10-Q_2026-09-30_inr-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 26–28, 30–31, 46, 50, 60

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The scenario starts with a gas price near the second- and third-quarter 2026 benchmarks of USD 2.90 and USD 2.96 per MMBtu persisting into 2027 while oil falls back toward the hedged level of USD 65.08, which is lower than the third-quarter benchmark of USD 87.22 per barrel. Realised prices and EBITDA fall, the hedges cushion roughly 39.98% of oil and 42.63% of gas volume, and the fixed charges of USD 74.3 million a year, the firm transportation agreement and the spending needed to hold acreage continue, so free cash flow stays negative and the revolver funds the gap. At the spring or autumn redetermination lenders can cut the base as reserve values fall, any excess could be repayable at once, and the leverage test of 3.0x applies on a definition that cannot be calculated here. Management's levers are to slow spending as operator, pay the preferred dividend in kind until its second anniversary and stop repurchases; on reported figures liquidity of USD 901.2 million, unchanged debt maturities and the wide EBITDA cushion suggest resilience is sufficient to avoid distress within 12 to 24 months, but the margin falls if the base and prices fall together.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation calc-cushion; calculation calc-hedge; calculation calc-fixed; 10-Q_2026-09-30_inr-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 27, 30–31, 37, 43, 46–47; 10-K_2025-12-31_inr-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 23, 75

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Overall, Infinity presents an adequate business profile supported by scale, high margins, low reported leverage and large liquidity, but credit quality is constrained by negative free cash flow, notes that rank behind a larger secured revolver, a preferred claim at the parent, concentrated customers and sponsor-controlled governance. Cash-flow durability appears adequate, because margins hold near two-thirds while spending is discretionary but partly committed to hold acreage. Refinancing capacity is likely to depend on the borrowing base, the facility maturity and the gas price. The primary downside path is a price fall that meets a borrowing base cut while fixed charges continue. No peer set was supplied, so the comparison with typical issuers in the sector is not established. Further analysis would require the financing documents, Antero run-rate earnings and the autumn base outcome.
